doc.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
doc.interviewee: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor

title: Keppard at the Coconut Grove with Tim Brown
summary: Taylor describes Keppard's season with Tim Brown's big band at the Coconut Grove in New York, dated about 1919.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But Joe was most of us more of a style. And Louis still is a blue chord man. And he was a blues artist chord. And a hot chord man. But Freddie was great on breaks. He was great on... I had some kind of a new sort of... He could blue also and some of the other things he could do. Now, another thing Freddie kept with you. I don't know whether it's on the record or not. They sent for Tim Brown. Sent for the farm at the... Oh... Coconut Grove in New York. Had a big band. And the rich, the millionaires came to his coconut grove. He was the biggest one of the spots of New York. And so, Tim Brown had heard of this Freddie Kaepern. And so, he went down to play this season. And he just was a rave there in the play. He was like New York. He was going back to Scaldrack in the first season.
Swetman told me that Freddie played with him for a while at a beach ballroom. And about 1919. Do you think that might have been the same time? Same period?
Yeah, that was... 1919 was there after the war. Yeah. About the same time.
So, maybe Swetman got him from...
From... Brown. Yeah. He had a... kind of a season with Tim Brown. Big Brown.
